why: DP over prefixes with a dictionary: ok[i] is true when some dictionary word ends at i and the prefix before it, ok[i - len(word)], was itself breakable. ok[0] = true.
hints: If s can be broken, its last word is some dictionary word w ending at the end of s. What must be true of the rest?
ok[i] = any(ok[i - len(w)] and s[i - len(w):i] == w for w in words). The base case ok[0] = true is the empty prefix.
Put words in a set and only try lengths that some word actually has (at most 100), so each i costs O(distinct lengths * length). Return ok[n].
pitfalls: Greedy longest match fails: 'aaaab' style traps.
Plain recursion without memo is exponential on 'aaaa...b'.
